name: Nikhilam Navatashcaramam Dashatah
meaning: All from 9 and the last from 10
use: Multiplying numbers near 10, 100 or 1000; complements; dividing by 9
method: Pick the base nearest to both numbers
Write each number's deviation (minus below the base, plus above)
Left part: one number plus the other's deviation
Right part: multiply the deviations, using as many digits as the base has zeros
watch: The right part must have exactly as many digits as the base has zeros: 12 for base 100, 012 for base 1000.

name: Yavadunam
meaning: Whatever the extent of its deficiency
use: Squares and cubes near a base; compound interest factors
method: Find the deviation d from the base
Left part: the number plus d
Right part: d², with the base's digit count
Carry any extra digit to the left
watch: A square uses the deviation once (n + d); the first part of a cube uses it twice (n + 2d).

name: Anurupyena
use: Numbers near 50, 200 or 500, where no power of 10 is close
method: Choose a working base, such as 50 = 100 ÷ 2
Cross-add as in Nikhilam
Scale the left part: halve it for 50, double it for 200
Right part: product of the deviations, two digits for base 100
watch: If halving leaves .5, drop it and add 50 to the right part.

name: Urdhva-Tiryagbhyam
use: Any multiplication; multiplying by 11; expanding algebraic products
method: Right: multiply the units digits
Middle: cross-multiply and add, plus the carry
Left: multiply the tens digits, plus the carry
watch: In 3-digit numbers the middle step has three products; skipping one is the commonest slip.
anim: Vertically on the right: 3 × 7 = 21 → write 1, carry 2

name: Ekadhikena Purvena
meaning: By one more than the previous one
use: Squaring numbers that end in 5; the decimal of 1/19
method: Take the part before the 5
Multiply it by one more than itself
Write 25 after the result
watch: The squaring rule works only for numbers ending in 5.
anim: A square ending in 5 always ends in 25

name: Antyayordashake'pi
meaning: When the last digits add up to 10
use: Two numbers with the same leading part whose last digits add to 10
method: Check: same leading part, last digits sum to 10
Left part: leading part × (itself + 1)
Right part: product of the last digits, always two digits
watch: Always write the right part with two digits: 09, not 9.

name: Ekanyunena Purvena
meaning: By one less than the previous one
method: Pad the number with zeros to match the count of nines
Left part: the number minus 1
Right part: its complement from 10, 100 or 1000
watch: Pad first: 47 × 999 must be worked as 047 × 999.

name: Dwandwa Yoga (duplex)
method: Duplex: D(a) = a², D(ab) = 2ab, D(abc) = 2ac + b²
Take duplexes right to left, then shrink back
Write one digit each step and carry the rest
watch: An n-digit number always takes 2n − 1 steps; count them to avoid skipping one.

name: Vilokanam
use: Square and cube roots of perfect powers; x + 1/x equations
method: The last digit gives the root's last digit (or two candidates)
The leading digits give the first part
For squares, compare with a × (a + 1) to choose
watch: Only for numbers known to be perfect squares or cubes.
anim: Ends in 6, so the root ends in 4 or 6
guided: 70 is below 72, so take the smaller candidate. Last digit?

name: Kevalaih Saptakam Gunyat
method: abcabc = abc × 1001, so it divides by 7, 11 and 13
For remainders, alternately subtract and add 3-digit groups
watch: If the alternating sum is negative, add the divisor until it is positive.
anim: Split into groups of three from the right

name: Gunitasamuccayah
meaning: The product of the sum is the sum of the product
use: Checking expansions and factorisations; eliminating options
method: Put x = 1 on both sides
The coefficient sums must match
If two options pass, test x = 2
watch: A pass does not prove an option right; a fail always proves it wrong.
anim: Both sides match, so the expansion passes

name: Beejank (digit-sum check)
use: Rejecting wrong options without full calculation
method: Reduce each number to one digit; treat 9 as 0
Do the same operation on the digit sums
Keep only options with the matching digit sum
watch: It cannot catch swapped digits, such as 9396 and 9369.
guided: Digit sum of 97, to one digit?

name: Sankalana-Vyavakalanabhyam
method: Add the equations to get x + y
Subtract them to get x − y
Add and halve for x; subtract and halve for y
watch: Subtract the constants in the same order as the equations.

name: Paravartya Yojayet
use: Dividing by numbers just above a base, such as 112
method: Write the excess over the base with signs changed
Bring down each quotient digit and spread its products
The last columns form the remainder
watch: If a column total goes negative, reduce the quotient by 1.
anim: Last column: 4 − 2 = 2, so the remainder is 02

name: Anurupye Shunyamanyat and Shunyam Samyasamuccaye
meaning: If one is in ratio, the other is zero; when the sum is the same, it is zero
use: Equations whose root can be read off
method: If one variable's coefficients match the ratio of the constants, the other variable is 0
If the same sum or product appears on both sides, set it to 0
watch: This finds one root; a quadratic may have another.
anim: So the other variable is zero: x = 0

name: Vestanam (osculation)
method: Find the osculator: 7 → 5, 13 → 4, 19 → 2
Multiply the last digit by it and add to the rest
Repeat until the number is small
watch: It tells you divisibility only, not the remainder.

name: Shesanyankena Charamena
meaning: The remainders by the last digit
method: List the remainders of 10, 100, 1000 … divided by the denominator
Multiply each by the denominator's last digit
Keep the last digits: they are the decimal
watch: The decimal rule works only for denominators ending in 3 or 7.

name: Dhvajanka (straight division)
use: Dividing by any two-digit number in one line
method: Split the divisor: main digit and flag (73 → 7, flag 3)
Divide by the main digit and carry the remainder
Before each step, subtract flag × the previous quotient digit
watch: If a net value goes negative, reduce the previous quotient digit by 1.

name: Puranapuranabhyam
use: Completing squares and cubes; powers of x + 1/x
method: Build the complete square or cube
Subtract the cross terms you did not want
watch: With x − 1/x, the sign changes: x² + 1/x² = (x − 1/x)² + 2.
